### Summary

The same deck on two devices does not give the same bits. The order in which a reduction adds its terms, the
fused operations a compiler emits, and the kernels a library picks all differ between a CPU and a GPU, so a
CPU run and a CUDA run of one build agree to round-off, not bit for bit. The report therefore states device
agreement in three tiers. Within one device, two runs of one build are compared bit for bit, and that is what
the bitwise gates rest on (@sec-ch16-gates). Between CUDA and the CPU, the shipped test compares a reconstruction
line by line to a fixed absolute tolerance, and the CUDA path's batched launch against its own one-variable
launch bit for bit. Between MPS and the CPU, which differ also in precision (MPS has no float64), every arm is
held to a relative tolerance tied to the CPU's own float32 error. @fig-ch16-evidence places these checks among
the two kinds of evidence the report uses.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** State what is compared across CPU, CUDA and MPS, and to what tolerance.

**Data.** Reads nothing; each test builds its own state on the devices it compares.

**Placement.** ctest entries: the CUDA line test only in a CUDA build, the MPS test in any build (it skips
without MPS).

**Activation.** The device of the block (`DEVICE`, or the tensors' device in a Python driver). Default: CPU.

**Guarantee / limits.** Bit for bit within one device and build; CUDA against CPU per reconstruction line to
$10^{-12}$ absolute; MPS against CPU to $\max(10^{-4}, 3\,\mathrm{err}_{64})$ relative per arm, and exactly for the
reconstruction arms. No test compares a whole CUDA run with a whole CPU run.

**Evidence.** `test_weno5_cuda_line.release` and `test_mps_matches_cpu_python` (@tbl-ch16-devices-tests).
:::

Local symbols of this section: $\mathrm{err}$ the relative error of one arm; $\mathrm{err}_{64}$ the same error of the CPU
float32 run against the CPU float64 run; $\mathrm{tol}$ the fixed floor $10^{-4}$.

### Derivation

**The MPS tolerance.** For one arm, with $q$ ranging over the arm's variables,

$$
\mathrm{err} = \max_q \frac{\max |q_{\mathrm{mps}} - q_{\mathrm{cpu}}|}{\max |q_{\mathrm{cpu}}|}, \qquad
\text{pass} \iff \mathrm{err} \le \max(\mathrm{tol},\ 3\,\mathrm{err}_{64}), \quad \mathrm{tol} = 10^{-4},
$$ {#eq-ch16-mps}

and both runs must be finite. MPS computes in float32, so it cannot be held to the CPU's float64 answer more
tightly than the CPU's own float32 run is: $\mathrm{err}_{64}$ measures that, on the same arm, and the factor 3 leaves room
for a different but equally valid order of float32 operations. The floor $\mathrm{tol}$ covers arms where $\mathrm{err}_{64}$ is
tiny. The reconstruction arms run the CPU kernel on MPS data, so they are held to $\mathrm{err} = 0$. The ripple arms compare
the tendency $u(n) - u(0)$ instead of the state, so that a small tendency is not hidden behind a large
background.

**The CUDA line tolerance.** One reconstruction call on the CPU and on CUDA, on the same float64 input, must agree
to $\max|r_{\mathrm{cuda}} - r_{\mathrm{cpu}}| < 10^{-12}$, an absolute bound. Within
CUDA, a call on many variables must equal, bit for bit, the same call on each variable alone, which is a
within-device statement and so exact.

### Numerical method

**CUDA.** `test_weno5_cuda_line.cpp` exists because a CUDA reconstruction launches one thread block per line, and
a line of more than 1024 cells must take a tiled path. It checks WENO5, WENO3 and the degree 3 and 5 polynomial
reconstructions on lines of 32, 1024, 1025, 1030 and 1280 cells against the CPU, and the many-variable launch
against single-variable launches, on uniform and stretched $x_1$ grids. It is registered only in a CUDA build and
skips its cases when no device is visible.

**MPS.** `test_mps_matches_cpu.py` runs each arm in float32 on the CPU and on MPS, and in float64 on the CPU for
$\mathrm{err}_{64}$: the reconstruction arms, a solid-cell arm, and deck arms: a dry state at rest and a dry bubble (with the
LMARS, HLLC and Roe solvers, other reconstructions, both implicit schemes and the face form of the gravity work),
two rippled states, and a moist column. The moist column stops before its last stage, where the saturation adjustment calls the thermodynamics
library, which has no MPS kernel. Two configurations must be refused on MPS with their messages: a stretched $x_1$
grid ("not supported on MPS") and anomaly storage ("MPS does not have", float64). Without MPS the test exits with
the skip code 125.

**Between CPU and CUDA runs of a whole deck.** No test, and no gate: the bitwise gates compare CPU with CPU and
CUDA with CUDA only, and their tools record a CPU-against-CUDA comparison as information.[^ch16-dev-src]

### Code

**How to use it.**

```sh
ctest -R 'test_weno5_cuda_line|test_mps_matches_cpu' --output-on-failure   # from the build directory
```

**What is refused, and why.** On MPS, a stretched $x_1$ grid and anomaly storage stop with an error instead of
falling back; @sec-ch17 lists both as limits and gives their homes. The MPS test checks that both refusals happen
and carry their messages.

The two tests are cited by file: {{< code tests/test_weno5_cuda_line.cpp >}} and
{{< code tests/test_mps_matches_cpu.py >}}; their registrations, the CUDA-only one and the skip code of the MPS
one, are in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_weno5_cuda_line.release` (CUDA builds only) | `recon_cuda.line_above_1024_matches_cpu`: each reconstruction on lines up to 1280 cells matches the CPU; `recon_cuda.many_variables_match_one_at_a_time` and its stretched-$x_1$ twin: a many-variable launch equals single-variable launches | `EXPECT_LT(diff, 1e-12)` (max absolute difference); `torch::equal` on the bit patterns | `expect_matches_cpu` and `expect_each_as_alone` ({{< code tests/test_weno5_cuda_line.cpp >}}) |
| `test_mps_matches_cpu_python` | every arm of @eq-ch16-mps passes and both runs are finite; the stretched-$x_1$ and anomaly configurations are refused with their messages; skipped (code 125) without MPS | $\mathrm{err} \le \max(10^{-4}, 3\,\mathrm{err}_{64})$ per arm; $\mathrm{err} = 0$ for the reconstruction arms | `TOL` and `main` ({{< code tests/test_mps_matches_cpu.py >}}) |

: Tests of device agreement and the tolerance each uses. {#tbl-ch16-devices-tests}

The MPS test's floor carries the comment that its worst arm measured $\mathrm{err} = 6.2\times10^{-6}$ on one Apple machine
with torch 2.10; this chapter did not rerun it (no MPS device was available).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No shipped test compares a whole CPU run with a whole CUDA run; agreement across those devices is stated per
  reconstruction line only.
- MPS runs float32 only and runs eager only; the moist column is compared before its saturation stage.
- The CUDA line test needs a CUDA device at run time; in a CUDA build on a machine without one its cases skip.
- Bit-for-bit agreement within a device assumes the same build, machine and library versions; another CPU (other
  SIMD paths) or another GPU may give the same build other bits.[^ch16-dev-src]
:::
